This document covers formatting rules that extend the base JSONHTL specification.
String values within JSONHTL may contain markdown inline formatting. For example, a paragraph string may include `backtick code`, **bold**, or *emphasis* using standard markdown syntax.
Where markdown and JSONHTL objects express the same thing, both are valid. For example, these are equivalent:
Similarly, a heading can be expressed as a JSONHTL block or as a markdown-formatted string within a
element, though the structured form is preferred for machine processing.

Tabular data uses the
block type. A table contains

Each cell value is either a string or a list of inline elements (the same content model as
). A string cell may contain markdown inline markup (bold, code, italic) as in
text. A list cell may contain structured inline objects — most usefully
— so a table cell can hold a clickable link exactly as a paragraph can. Renderers must handle both cell forms; a bare string and a single-element inline list wrapping that string are equivalent.
This structure maps directly to a Pandas DataFrame:

codeblock.body:
import pandas as pd
table = block["table"]
df = pd.DataFrame(table["rows"], columns=table["columns"])

para: And back again:
The Pandas mapping above assumes scalar (string) cells. When a cell is an inline-element list,
stores the list itself as the cell value; consumers doing tabular analysis should flatten such cells to their concatenated text first.
Tables should be used for genuinely tabular data. For simple key-value pairs where only two columns exist, a series of
blocks may be clearer. Use judgement.
